sections.title: Tree and leaves
sections.text: Tamarindus indica is a long-lived tropical tree, up to about 30 m tall, with a spreading crown that may reach 12 m across. Its finely divided leaves are up to 15 cm long, with many pairs of small leaflets; the plate shows the characteristic compound leaf.

sections.title: Flowers and pods
sections.text: The yellow flowers, veined red, are about 2.5 cm across. Curved, brown, sausage-shaped pods hold sticky, acidic pulp around hard seeds; fruits are commonly 5–15 cm long. These features match the plate.

sections.title: Food and uses
sections.text: The ripe pulp is widely eaten raw or used in curries, pickles, sweets and drinks; Kew also records seeds eaten raw or cooked. A regional Indian source records young leaves and flowers used as vegetables. The wood is also used for timber and fuel.

sources.title: Tamarindus indica — Plants of the World Online, Kew
